newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - French GDP shrank 0.4 pct in Q2.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - French GDP shrank 0.4 pct in Q2.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments after national statistics institute INSEE announced that French gross domestic product shrank 0.4 percent in the second quarter from the first quarter.
Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a fall 0.2-0.4 percent.

The numbers have come in on the soft side of expectations, not only with the Q2 figures but also with the downwards revision of the first quarter. It makes it look more likely rather than less likely that the government's targets on growth will be hit this year and emphasises the difficulties in hitting this year's deficit targets.

It's reasonable to expect a bounceback in the third quarter. You are looking at a recovery of the fall in the second quarter and maybe a little bit more depending on how much the car incentive scheme boosts consumption ahead of (the expiry of the scheme) at the end of September.
It is a bit of a surprise that it falls that much. As much as 0.5 percentage points comes from the (smaller) number of working days.

I believe the third quarter may be quite strong. The worse the number in Q2 the stronger it will be in Q3. The most recent numbers we have got for July and August (car sales) suggest consumer spending will rebound enormously after the dive in Q2. It may be almost as strong as two percent.
Overall I still believe the French economy is growing at a pace of two percent on the underlying trend, and maybe a bit less in the first half, which is just about enough to stabilise unemployment.

The main problem now is Q4. With all the gloom we have at the moment, the risk is that we have a bad Q4 because of the confidence factor. It makes the three percent (1997 budget deficit/GDP ratio) a bit more risky. But at the moment three percent seems to me quite credible.
This is quite alarming. Clearly this is going to weigh on the deficit problem. The (bond market) reaction is more likely to be negative than positive.
